judul: The Smiling Man of Maple Hollow

baris.text: In Maple Hollow, Vermont... nobody locked their doors.
Not the Hendersons. Not the Parkers. Not even old Mr. Miller, who lived alone at the end of Elm Street.
That changed on the night of December fourteenth. The night the Smiling Man came to town.
It was eleven forty-seven p.m. when Jake and Emily Carter missed the last bus home from the Winter Fair.
Jake was seventeen, tired, and in charge of getting his little sister home. Emily was sixteen... and she would not stop talking.
Okay, admit it. I totally beat you at the ring toss.
You threw the ring at the guy's head, Em.
And it landed! That counts!
It does not count.
Hey... did you hear what Tyler said at the fair? About the Smiling Man?
Tyler also said he saw Bigfoot behind the Walmart.
He said the Smiling Man only follows you if you look at him. And once he starts following you... he never stops.
Em. It's a story. Somebody made it up to scare little kids.
Jake was right about one thing. Somebody did make up the story of the Smiling Man. But that didn't mean he wasn't real.
The fastest way home was Elm Street. Down past the harbor, past the old houses... past Mr. Miller's place.
Mr. Miller was always awake. Always on his porch. Always... watching.
Evening, kids. Awful cold night to be walking alone.
Uh... evening, Mr. Miller.
You two get home quick now. Don't stop. And don't talk to anybody.
Okay. That was the creepiest thing he has ever said. And he has said a lot of creepy things.
Just keep walking.
The snow was falling harder now. The streetlights hummed. And somewhere behind them... something crunched.
One footstep. Then another. Slow. Heavy. Like someone dragging something through the snow.
Jake... do you hear that?
It's probably just Mr. Miller.
It wasn't Mr. Miller.
At the end of the street, under the last working streetlight, stood a man in a black hood.
His face was a white porcelain mask, cracked down one side. Someone had painted a smile on it. A big, red, stitched-up smile.
And in his right hand... he was holding an axe.
Is that... a Halloween thing? Like a prank?
Em. It's December.
The man tilted his head. Slowly. Like he was trying to remember their faces.
Then he took one step forward.
Run!
They ran. Past the bakery, past the church, past houses where every single window was dark.
Jake, call somebody! Call Mom!
I'm trying! There's no signal!
Jake's phone buzzed. A text from Mom... sent twenty minutes ago.
Where are you two? The news said a patient escaped from Ravenwood Hospital. Do not walk home.
Jake looked back.
The man wasn't running. He was walking. Calm. Patient... like he already knew where they were going.
But they had one advantage. They knew Maple Hollow. Every alley. Every shortcut. Every fence with a hole in it.
The harbor! We can lose him at the harbor!
Em, keep the flashlight down. Don't let him see the light!
Okay... okay!
They cut down to the harbor and ducked behind a row of old shipping crates, frozen solid with ice.
Is he gone? Jake... is he gone?
Shh. Don't move. Don't breathe.
Jake counted his heartbeats. Ten. Twenty. Thirty. Maybe he was gone. Maybe they had lost him.
Crunch. Crunch. Crunch.
The footsteps came closer. Then they stopped. Right on the other side of the crates.
They could hear him breathing. Slow, wet breaths behind the mask.
And then... Jake's phone buzzed.
Found you.
Go! Go! Go!
They ran out onto the pier, toward the old ship. Jake dialed nine-one-one with shaking fingers.
Nine-one-one, what is your emergency?
There's a man with an axe! He's chasing us! We're at the harbor on Elm Street!
Okay. Stay calm. Officers are on the way. They're about twelve minutes out.
Twelve minutes? Jake, we don't have twelve minutes!
Behind them, the Smiling Man stepped onto the pier. The old boards groaned under his boots.
There was only one way out. Back across the frozen pond... toward Mr. Miller's house.
Everybody in Maple Hollow knew the rule. Never cross the pond after the ice cutters had been out.
The ice was cut into blocks. Thin in some places. Gone in others.
There's no other way, Em. Whatever happens, do not stop running.
Jake, the ice... it's cracking!
Step where I step. Just step where I step!
They ran. The ice groaned. Cracks shot out under their feet like lightning.
And behind them, the Smiling Man followed. Heavier. Slower.
Halfway across, he stopped. He looked down.
Crack.
The ice gave way. And the Smiling Man dropped into the black water without a sound.
Is he... is he gone?
The water rippled. Then it went still. Nothing came back up.
He's gone, Jake. He's really gone.
Come on. Let's get out of here.
Mr. Miller was waiting on his porch, holding the door open.
In. Both of you. Now!
Sirens finally echoed down Elm Street. Red and blue lights flashed across the snow.
I saw him following you. Saw him from my window. That's why I told you not to stop.
We thought... we thought you were the creepy one.
Son, I'm eighty-one years old. I'm allowed to be a little creepy.
And for the first time all night... Emily laughed.
Thank you, Mr. Miller. Really.
The police searched the pond until sunrise. They found the axe. They found the hole in the ice.
But they never found the man.
Ravenwood Hospital never released the patient's real name. The night staff only ever called him one thing... the Smiling Man.
Three nights later, Jake's phone buzzed. A message from an unknown number.
Jake... who is that from?
In Maple Hollow, Vermont... everybody locks their doors now.
But a lock only works... if he's still outside.
